note: Slice 1 of docs/specs/routed-writes.md: whether a write sent to a resident daemon saves time over a direct write. It does not, so routed writes are not pursued.
fixtures: mdb-10k/collection and mdb-100k/collection from scripts/generate_mdb_fixture.py (generator v1, seed 42), scanned with `scan --full`

machine.host: development laptop, not the designated evaluation host (Intel Core i7-8650U, 31 GiB RAM, Debian 13)

setup: Isolated XDG_CONFIG_HOME, XDG_STATE_HOME, XDG_DATA_HOME, and XDG_CACHE_HOME; daemon.toml binds 127.0.0.1:0
Direct runs first with no daemon, then both fixtures registered with `vault add --no-sync`, `daemon start --detach`, both caches fresh, and an API token per vault

The daemon side is measured through the existing REST write routes, which run the same workflow behind the host's mutation permit that a routed CLI write would; a routed CLI write would add the process floor and request encoding

method.timing: wall clock from Python; 11 runs per case, the first discarded; p50 and max of 10

findings: Daemon-side writes cost the same as direct ones at both sizes (REST set at 10K varied between runs, max 2,216 ms), so adding the process floor a routed write would be no faster.
Skipping the client's freshness proof (`--refresh off`) saves nothing: the cost is inside the write workflow both paths share.

Ordinary note writes refresh the cache with a full incremental scan, which discovers every file (about 500 ms at 100K even when nothing changed) and then refreshes vault-wide derived state. vulcan_core::scan::scan_vault_paths_unlocked already limits a scan to the paths a writer touched, and mdbase writes and the editor use it; note writes do not.
decision: Routed writes are not pursued. The shared write path's post-write refresh is the cost every integration pays, and fixing it directly benefits direct, MCP, REST, and daemon writes alike.
